nd-205-ret: equivalent: gshscene_node_canonical is called only from gshscene_edit_add and gshscene_edit_set, each of which returns INVALID for no properties before it (tests/unit/test_edit.cpp, EditAdd.ANodeNeedsItsPropertiesAndNamesNoPlane...: add and set with NULL props are INVALID), so its own refusal of none is never reached through the API
df-447-del: equivalent: the plane branch of the damage is not reachable: a node names no plane as its region or clip (check_region refuses it; witness in the same test: a shape of a plane and a group clipped by a plane are not OK), so a damage never meets a plane resource
bg-570-and: equivalent: the line is reached only for a fill whose paint has a resource (the line above returns for none) that is not a pattern or a hatch; the list refuses a paint whose resource is of another kind than the paint says (witness: test_dump_sink.cpp, DumpSink.ANullListHoldsNothingAndAPaintWhoseResourceIsOfAnotherKindIsRefused), so `paint.kind == GRADIENT` and `resource->kind == GRADIENT` are the same test and && and || agree
ds-2104-and: equivalent: with || the walk of a picture runs for every item that is not refused; for an item that is not an instance gshscene_resource_picture is NULL (it returns the list only for a picture resource, which only an instance carries), and cache_list of NULL visits no item (witness: gshscene_list_count(NULL) == 0, same test as bg-570-and)
fp-equal-picture: equivalent: the canonical string holds the picture's content hash, so two filters with different pictures differ in the string before the handle comparison is reached; the handle decides only on a hash collision, as for an image's (FL12, a hash never decides)
fp-slot-needs-picture: equivalent: without the guard a slot with no picture reaches gshscene_list_count(gshscene_resource_picture(NULL)), which is 0, so the bound `slot >= 0` refuses it all the same (witness: test_filter_picture.cpp, TheRefusalsInTheirOrder, a slot without a picture)
lt-match-style: equivalent: gshscene_linetype_matches runs only for resources of one content hash, and the hash covers every element string, so two linetypes that differ in a style never meet it (witness: test_linetype EveryFieldIsPartOfTheContent gives distinct handles for each differing field)
lt-match-mode: equivalent: the hash covers the rotation mode, so the match is reached only for equal modes (witness: EveryFieldIsPartOfTheContent)
lt-match-offset: equivalent: the hash covers both offsets, so the match is reached only for equal offsets (witness: EveryFieldIsPartOfTheContent)
lt-match-description: equivalent: the hash covers the description, so the match is reached only for equal descriptions (witness: EveryFieldIsPartOfTheContent)
st-hash-linetype: equivalent: the style match also compares the linetype handle, so a style that differs only by linetype is still a distinct resource when the hash agrees; only the hash bucket changes
st-match-linetype: equivalent: the style hash includes the linetype handle, so styles that differ only by linetype never reach the match (witness: StylesDifferByLinetypeEvenWhenTheirDashesAgree in test_linetype)
st-linetype-kind: not caught, argued: the check guards reading another kind's resource through the linetype union; a path resource named as a linetype is refused by the later checks in the witness (AReadOfAnythingButALinetype... test), but what the plant lets through reads a union member of the wrong kind, which no test can pin without undefined behavior
st-release-linetype: equivalent for every observable: the style does not own a reference count that any API exposes, the store frees all resources at its end, and a leak check (ASan, Valgrind in the gates) is what sees it
